dep/include/utf8cpp/doc/utf8cpp.html : The library was designed to be:
dep/include/utf8cpp/doc/utf8cpp.html : Generic: for better or worse, there are many C++ string classes out there, and
dep/include/utf8cpp/doc/utf8cpp.html : the library should work with as many of them as possible.
dep/include/utf8cpp/doc/utf8cpp.html : Portable: the library should be portable both accross different platforms and
dep/include/utf8cpp/doc/utf8cpp.html : compilers. The only non-portable code is a small section that declares unsigned
dep/include/utf8cpp/doc/utf8cpp.html : integers of different sizes: three typedefs. They can be changed by the users of
dep/include/utf8cpp/doc/utf8cpp.html : the library if they don't match their platform. The default setting should work
dep/include/utf8cpp/doc/utf8cpp.html : for Windows (both 32 and 64 bit), and most 32 bit and 64 bit Unix derivatives.
dep/include/utf8cpp/doc/utf8cpp.html : Lightweight: follow the "pay only for what you use" guidline.
dep/include/utf8cpp/doc/utf8cpp.html : Unintrusive: avoid forcing any particular design or even programming style on the
dep/include/utf8cpp/doc/utf8cpp.html : user. This is a library, not a framework.
dep/include/utf8cpp/doc/utf8cpp.html : In case you want to look into other means of working with UTF-8 strings from C++,
dep/include/utf8cpp/doc/utf8cpp.html : here is the list of solutions I am aware of:
dep/include/utf8cpp/doc/utf8cpp.html : ICU Library. It is very powerful,
dep/include/utf8cpp/doc/utf8cpp.html : complete, feature-rich, mature, and widely used. Also big, intrusive,
dep/include/utf8cpp/doc/utf8cpp.html : non-generic, and doesn't play well with the Standard Library. I definitelly
dep/include/utf8cpp/doc/utf8cpp.html : recommend looking at ICU even if you don't plan to use it.

dep/include/utf8cpp/doc/utf8cpp.html : code, it may be worth a look. Be aware of the licensing issues, though.
dep/include/utf8cpp/doc/utf8cpp.html : Platform dependent solutions: Windows and POSIX have functions to convert strings
